source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: DeepSeek correctly does not execute a TBD row but misses that the title maps to standard read-only App command 44h; it therefore does not separate known mechanics from the missing channel, user scope and security-policy acceptance.

original_test_intent.purpose: Validate the BMC's out-of-band Get User Access implementation for an approved channel/user scope by decoding user-slot counts, enable state, authentication/messaging access and privilege limit, then comparing them with the channel and account security policy without changing access state.
original_test_intent.target: The exact BMC/firmware reached through protected OOB IPMI, for a finite owner-approved set of channel numbers and nonzero User IDs; this command does not return a username or password.
original_test_intent.scope: For each signed channel/User-ID pair, send App command 44h, validate the five response data bytes after completion, decode maximum/enabled/fixed-name counts and per-user access fields under the applicable IPMI errata behavior, and cross-check the effective privilege against Get Channel Access. Do not enumerate unapproved accounts or call any setter.
original_test_intent.operation: Verify BMC identity and secure transport; run `ipmitool raw 0x06 0x44 <channel> <user-id>` for only the approved pairs; parse reserved bits, counts, enable state, callback restriction, link-authentication, IPMI-messaging and user privilege; separately read the channel privilege limit because a successful response does not report an over-privileged mismatch; compare with the signed policy and store redacted evidence.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: The workbook estimates 10 attended and 5 machine minutes but defines no channel/user matrix. V3 requires a finite signed matrix and does not infer one representative account or authorize scanning all slots.
original_test_intent.expected_result: Every approved pair returns a structurally valid response consistent with the BMC's IPMI errata behavior; aggregate counts are self-consistent; per-user enable/access/privilege matches the security baseline; effective privilege does not exceed the channel limit; no user, password, channel or session policy changes.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: BMC/firmware/IPMI revision and secure-session identity; signed channel/User-ID matrix and policy; exact redacted requests/responses/completion/length; decoded maximum, enabled and fixed-name counts; errata-aware User-ID status and access bits; Get Channel Access comparison; exception handling and non-mutation audit.
ambiguities: Procedure and Criteria are TBD and do not specify a channel, User ID set, expected access policy or whether one account or all approved accounts are in scope.
IPMI pre-errata-3 and errata-3-or-later implementations differ in how enable status and bits 5:4 are interpreted.
Get User Access alone does not identify usernames and does not guarantee the user's privilege is no higher than the channel privilege limit.
The source's generic log-clearing step is unrelated to this read and would remove security audit evidence.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly identifies standard read-only 06h/44h, protected OOB transport, redaction, full field parsing, channel-policy comparison and the no-set boundary. It calls the complete test FULLY AUTOMATABLE while requiring an approved user/channel and policy that the TBD source does not supply, assumes one user without source support, and omits the response's aggregate slot counts and IPMI errata-3 enable-status distinction.

applicable_history.decision: No locked user decision supplies a channel/User-ID matrix or expected access baseline. Historical FULL treatment is review evidence, not authorization to enumerate accounts.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Reclassify FULLY AUTOMATABLE to REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION. The read and parser are automatable, but the complete security-policy test requires an owner-supplied finite channel/User-ID matrix, applicable errata behavior and expected access baseline. No mutation approval is needed after those inputs.

available_now: IPMI 2.0 section 22.27 defines App command 44h, its two request bytes and five returned access/count bytes.
BMC identity, channel inventory and parser behavior can be checked without querying unapproved user IDs or changing configuration.
The read can be correlated with standard Get Channel Access to detect an effective privilege limit mismatch.
missing_inputs: Finite approved channel/User-ID matrix, purpose of each account class and whether disabled/fixed-name/null-user slots are included
Expected security baseline for enable state, callback restriction, link authentication, IPMI messaging and privilege plus applicable IPMI errata/firmware behavior
Expected maximum/enabled/fixed-name counts and exception policy; channel privilege baseline for effective-access comparison
Qualified protected `lanplus`/raw runner, credential source, target identity validation, redaction and audit-retention policy
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The BMC/IAM owner supplies the approved channel/User-ID scope and security baseline; the firmware owner states applicable errata behavior; the lab/tool owner supplies protected transport, parser and evidence handling.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Record BMC/firmware/IPMI identity, documented channels and current channel-access limits through approved non-mutating queries.
Offline-test response parsing for pre-errata-3 and later layouts, reserved bits, slot counts, privileges and malformed responses with synthetic data.
prohibited_until_closed: Do not scan all user IDs/channels, guess account scope, request User ID 0, disclose usernames or access topology, use insecure command-line credentials, call Set User Access/Name/Password/Payload Access or clear security logs.
Do not treat command success as policy compliance or ignore a user privilege that exceeds the channel limit because the BMC may not return an error for that mismatch.
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: Owners sign the finite matrix, expected policy/counts and errata behavior; protected OOB transport and redaction are tested; the parser covers all five response bytes; channel-limit comparison is included; evidence proves no setter or broad enumeration is issued.

revision_candidate.test_name: OOB IPMI Get User Access for an Approved Channel/User Matrix
revision_candidate.purpose: Read and validate the configured access state and effective privilege policy for each approved BMC channel/User-ID pair through protected OOB IPMI without changing any account or channel setting.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: The exact BMC/IPMI firmware with protected `lanplus` access, known errata behavior, approved management channels and a signed non-secret User-ID scope; evidence access is restricted as security metadata.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Only the signed nonzero User IDs on approved channels. Unapproved enumeration, usernames/passwords, payload access and all account/channel mutations are outside scope.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: BMC/firmware/IPMI/errata identity; channel/User-ID matrix; expected maximum/enabled/fixed-name counts; per-pair access and privilege policy; channel privilege limits; qualified runner/parser; protected credentials; redaction, exception and retention rules.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Verify the BMC and secure OOB session. For each approved pair, execute `ipmitool raw 0x06 0x44 <channel> <user-id>`, require successful completion and five data bytes, validate reserved bits, decode aggregate counts and errata-aware enable/access/privilege fields, read the corresponding channel access limit, compare all fields with policy, and archive redacted evidence without invoking any setter.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Correct BMC and channel verified; signed scope and policy present; nonzero User IDs valid for the channel; applicable firmware/errata behavior known; credentials protected; parser/redaction tested; security logs preserved; no concurrent account changes.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Verified target/firmware/tool/session identity; signed scope; redacted exact requests/responses; completion and five-byte length; decoded aggregate counts and per-user fields; channel privilege comparison; policy result and exceptions; non-mutation/audit evidence.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: Intel IPMI 2.0 rev. 1.1 section 22.27/Table 22-32 and Get Channel Access rules, plus the exact BMC firmware's errata behavior and owner-approved channel/account security baseline.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Never scan unapproved accounts, disclose credentials/usernames/policy details, use User ID 0, ignore channel privilege precedence, change access/password/name/payload settings, clear logs or auto-remediate a mismatch.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: No runtime mutation approval is required for authorized reads. The BMC/IAM owner must provide the missing finite scope, expected policy and evidence handling rules before execution.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Owners define authorized account scope, expected security policy and exception disposition. The agent can then perform bounded reads, decode all fields, compare channel precedence and produce redacted evidence; remediation is a separate approved case.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: No recovery is expected. On target/scope mismatch, malformed output, policy conflict or sensitive-data exposure, stop, preserve restricted evidence, close the session and escalate; never change the account automatically.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Missing signed scope/policy; wrong BMC/channel; User ID 0; unapproved enumeration; unknown errata behavior that changes interpretation; insecure credentials/redaction; nonzero completion; response not five data bytes; reserved value; inconsistent counts; privilege-policy conflict; concurrent account change; or any setter request.

identified_defects: V2's FULLY AUTOMATABLE label conflicts with the missing channel/User-ID and policy inputs it requires.
V2 invents a single-user scope instead of requiring a finite owner-selected matrix.
V2 omits maximum/enabled/fixed-name response counts and the errata-3 enable-status interpretation.
The source has no policy acceptance criteria and includes inappropriate log clearing.
reason_for_change: Preserve the standard read-only implementation while applying V3's boundary between automation capability and missing engineer inputs. A security-sensitive account query cannot be called fully automatable when its authorized target matrix and expected policy are absent, but those obtainable inputs do not make it BLOCKED.

new_technical_evidence.title: Intelligent Platform Management Interface Specification v2.0 rev. 1.1 E7 Markup
new_technical_evidence.applicability: BMCs implementing standard App command 44h on the selected channel
new_technical_evidence.supports: Get User Access returns maximum, enabled and fixed-name user counts plus callback restriction, link-authentication, IPMI-messaging and privilege state. Enable-status interpretation differs for pre-errata-3 implementations, and software must compare user privilege with the channel limit because the BMC need not error on a mismatch.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: Authorized channel/User-ID scope, expected policy, firmware errata behavior and account-class exceptions remain owner inputs.

removed_ambiguities: Defines the complete five-byte response rather than only generic access fields.
Separates per-user privilege from the effective channel privilege ceiling.
Makes the authorized account matrix explicit and prohibits inferred enumeration.
resolved_blockers: Standard command framing and field meanings are known and safely automatable once the authorized scope/policy is supplied.
remaining_blockers: Execution remains pending a finite approved channel/User-ID matrix, expected security baseline, applicable errata behavior and protected evidence policy.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 prevents unauthorized or arbitrary account selection, adds the missing aggregate/errata fields and channel-precedence check, while retaining a non-mutating automatable reader after owner inputs are available.

agent_understanding_result.notes: The FULLY-to-REQUIRES reclassification and account-scope/errata contract are queued for isolated understanding validation.
